The brokerage's view rests on a steep fall in Chinese diesel shipments and dwindling stocks in major consuming markets, which together could leave buyers competing for fewer barrels. That outlook contrasts with a weaker picture for India's upstream producers, whose shares have trailed global peers.

China's diesel exports are expected to drop below 0.8mn tonnes in November 2026, compared with 1.33mn tonnes in August and 1.8mn tonnes in September, according to Equirus's latest Oil & Gas Weekly Tracker. Commercial diesel stocks in China stood at 11.1mn tonnes at the end of October, the lowest since records started in 2011.
Diesel inventories are also falling in the United States and other large markets, the brokerage said. It named standalone refiners such as Reliance as the main winners from the squeeze.

Diesel cracks, the gap between crude prices and refined diesel prices that shows how much refiners earn from processing crude, have already lifted profitability, Equirus noted. It expects continued tightness in the diesel market to stay favourable for Indian refiners, whatever happens to crude.

Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) and Oil India have lagged international energy companies, the report said. Investors are worried about government intervention, weak output growth and whether the two firms can keep the gains from higher crude prices.

Equirus pointed to earlier periods of high prices, when upstream companies provided crude discounts to oil marketing companies, and to the windfall taxes introduced in 2022. Fears that extra profits could end up being shared with the government continue to weigh on investor sentiment, the brokerage said.
Production growth at ONGC has been muted. Natural declines at existing fields and delays in starting new projects have limited how far upstream firms can raise output, according to the report.

Equirus also flagged tight global gas markets as a factor for the coming quarters. Europe's gas storage was about 71% full, with net withdrawals already underway, and inventories sat materially below seasonal averages.

title: Indian refiners set to benefit from tight diesel supply
